items.title: Decolonisation of Africa

edges.quote: Italy, a colonial power, lost its African empire, Italian East Africa, Italian Ethiopia, Italian Eritrea, Italian Somalia and Italian Libya, as a result of World War II.
edges.explanation: The article "Decolonisation of Africa" (revision 1379719162) states: "Italy, a colonial power, lost its African empire, Italian East Africa, Italian Ethiopia, Italian Eritrea, Italian Somalia and Italian Libya, as a result of World War II." The loss it names is part of what this record is: the edge reads that sentence and nothing more, and the scope the sentence gives it is Italy's empire.

items.why: Africa trails at 327 active against the Americas' 431; decolonisation-of-africa is a held umbrella with no edge at all, and its own article states the cause of the Italian empire's end.

items.title: Scramble for Africa

edges.quote: After the Independence of Brazil in 1822, Portugal sought to protect, develop and expand its remaining overseas territories in order to compensate for the loss of Brazilian trade and revenue and its international standing, leading to an aggressive expansion of its Angolan and Mozambican territories.
edges.explanation: The article "Scramble for Africa" (revision 1376647971) states: "After the Independence of Brazil in 1822, Portugal sought to protect, develop and expand its remaining overseas territories in order to compensate for the loss of Brazilian trade and revenue and its international standing, leading to an aggressive expansion of its Angolan and Mozambican territories." The expansion it names is Portugal's share of the scramble, which is what this record holds; the edge reads that sentence and nothing more.

edges.quote: The tensions between the imperial powers led to a succession of crises, which exploded in August 1914, when previous rivalries and alliances created a domino situation that drew the major European nations into World War I.
edges.explanation: The article "Scramble for Africa" (revision 1376647971) states: "The tensions between the imperial powers led to a succession of crises, which exploded in August 1914, when previous rivalries and alliances created a domino situation that drew the major European nations into World War I." The tensions are the scramble's own, in the scramble's own article; precondition-of and not caused, because the sentence makes the rivalry what the crises grew out of.

items.why: Africa trails, and scramble-for-africa is a held umbrella carrying no edge: its own article states both what drove Portugal into it and what the imperial rivalry led to.

items.title: 12-3 incident

edges.quote: Portuguese sovereignty over Macau severely diminished after the incident, leading to de facto Chinese suzerainty over the territory 33 years prior to the eventual handover of Macau.
edges.explanation: The article "12-3 incident" (revision 1377636747) states: "Portuguese sovereignty over Macau severely diminished after the incident, leading to de facto Chinese suzerainty over the territory 33 years prior to the eventual handover of Macau." The sentence dates the end of effective Portuguese rule to the incident and the handover 33 years after it, which is a precondition and not a cause.

items.why: Asia trails at 327, and this is Portuguese history, which is the atlas's own subject: the incident's own article states that Portuguese sovereignty ended there, 33 years before the handover.

items.title: Fontainebleau Agreements

edges.quote: Generally the tough stance of both sides led to the First Indochina War between them on December 19.
edges.explanation: The article "Fontainebleau Agreements" (revision 1312816323) states: "Generally the tough stance of both sides led to the First Indochina War between them on December 19." The both sides are the two at Fontainebleau, in the conference's own article; the edge reads that sentence and nothing more.

items.why: Asia trails, first-indochina-war is a held umbrella with fewer than three children, and the conference's own article states that the stance taken there led to the war. Filed under no umbrella: the talks preceded the war and are not part of it.

items.title: Operation Searchlight

edges.quote: The widespread violence resulting from Pakistan's Operation Searchlight ultimately led to the Bangladesh Liberation War, in which Mukti Bahini guerrillas fought to remove Pakistani forces from East Pakistan.
edges.explanation: The article "Operation Searchlight" (revision 1374712761) states: "The widespread violence resulting from Pakistan's Operation Searchlight ultimately led to the Bangladesh Liberation War, in which Mukti Bahini guerrillas fought to remove Pakistani forces from East Pakistan." The operation's own article states the link; queued with no umbrella on purpose, because filing it under the war it led to would make the edge an edge from a parent to its own child (A14, C8 undecided).

items.why: Asia trails and bangladesh-liberation-war is a held umbrella with one child. The 12 October fire found this sentence and refused it under A14 because it filed the item under that war; with no parent the edge stands and the filing waits for C8.

items.title: Taliban insurgency

edges.quote: The end of the Taliban insurgency resulted in the beginning of a new insurgency against the restored Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan by the National Resistance Front and allied groups which fight under the banner of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan.
edges.explanation: The article "Taliban insurgency" (revision 1379529630) states: "The end of the Taliban insurgency resulted in the beginning of a new insurgency against the restored Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan by the National Resistance Front and allied groups which fight under the banner of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan." The insurgency's own article states what its end began; the two are siblings under war-in-afghanistan-2001-2021 and afghan-conflict, so the edge is not one from a parent to its own child.

items.why: Asia trails at 327, and war-in-afghanistan-2001-2021 is a held umbrella with one child (A6): this is a P361 child of it whose own article states a cause reaching outside the umbrella, which is what A15(5) leaves room for.
